svg.title: A Single Cohort, Five Observable Outcomes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-nested-enterprise-account-cohort; chart type: funnel; title: A Single Cohort, Five Observable Outcomes; subtitle: Track client-account pairs instead of mixing contacts, meetings, and deals.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative annual cohort across nine operator clients, followed through a full observation window. Each unit is one unique client-account pair, and each later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Count at most one qualifying opportunity and one downstream win per pair. Counts are planning assumptions, not measured benchmarks. Downstream customer wins may occur after the opportunity-fee recognition period.; caption: Base revenue bridge: nine clients paying $60,000 in earned annual retainers produce $540,000; 90 accepted opportunities at $1,500 produce $135,000; total operator revenue is $675,000.; stages: label: Eligible target pairs; value: 2,400 client-account pairs enter the defined annual cohort.; numeric value: 2400.0; detail: Create stable client-account identifiers, verify account fit, and exclude suppression records and existing opportunities barred by the attribution agreement.; label: Meaningfully engaged pairs; value: 600 pairs engage; 25.0% of eligible target pairs.; numeric value: 600.0; detail: Require a substantive response or documented buying interaction. Email delivery, tracking-pixel activity, and bot-generated clicks do not qualify as engagement.; label: Attended discovery pairs; value: 180 pairs attend discovery; 30.0% of engaged pairs.; numeric value: 180.0; detail: Require an attended session with a relevant buying role. Reschedules and repeated meetings retain the same pair identifier and do not increase the cohort count.; label: Accepted opportunity pairs; value: 90 pairs qualify; 50.0% of attended discovery pairs.; numeric value: 90.0; detail: Client acceptance must satisfy the contracted rubric and attribution rules. These 90 billable events support the $135,000 opportunity-fee component of the Base illustration.; label: Client contract wins; value: 18 pairs become customers; 20.0% of accepted opportunities.; numeric value: 18.0; detail: Record downstream wins to evaluate delivery quality. The resulting customer contract values belong to clients and contribute zero additional operator revenue in this model.

text.title: A Single Cohort, Five Observable Outcomes
text.tspan: A Single Cohort, Five Observable Outcomes

rect.title: label: Eligible target pairs; value: 2,400 client-account pairs enter the defined annual cohort.; numeric value: 2400.0; detail: Create stable client-account identifiers, verify account fit, and exclude suppression records and existing opportunities barred by the attribution agreement.

label: Meaningfully engaged pairs; value: 600 pairs engage; 25.0% of eligible target pairs.; numeric value: 600.0; detail: Require a substantive response or documented buying interaction. Email delivery, tracking-pixel activity, and bot-generated clicks do not qualify as engagement.

label: Attended discovery pairs; value: 180 pairs attend discovery; 30.0% of engaged pairs.; numeric value: 180.0; detail: Require an attended session with a relevant buying role. Reschedules and repeated meetings retain the same pair identifier and do not increase the cohort count.

label: Accepted opportunity pairs; value: 90 pairs qualify; 50.0% of attended discovery pairs.; numeric value: 90.0; detail: Client acceptance must satisfy the contracted rubric and attribution rules. These 90 billable events support the $135,000 opportunity-fee component of the Base illustration.

label: Client contract wins; value: 18 pairs become customers; 20.0% of accepted opportunities.; numeric value: 18.0; detail: Record downstream wins to evaluate delivery quality. The resulting customer contract values belong to clients and contribute zero additional operator revenue in this model.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative annual cohort across nine operator clients, followed through a full observation window. Each unit is one unique client-account pair, and each later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Count at most one qualifying opportunity and one downstream win per pair. Counts are planning assumptions, not measured benchmarks. Downstream customer wins may occur after the opportunity-fee recognition period.
